stage1.impression: A quiet night detail: a hammered copper bowl with a handful of red and clear discs on a pale timber shelf, a dark board-formed wall behind, and a soft-focus shopfront with street bokeh to the right. The bowl's metal is close to photographic, but the pale, smooth, stretched-grain shelf is the brightest thing in the frame, the bowl reads near empty, the coins carry dotted CG highlights, and half the frame is an unlit wall and a flat grey window. As it stands it is a generic still life by a window, not a specific place: nothing says EARF or Planet EARF, so a magazine would not run it as this bar.

blocking_9: The bowl and coins must be the brightest, most legible thing in the frame. Today the shelf front (median 133) and the window's lower band (median 122) outshine the bowl (median 28 to 40).
The bowl must read as full (40 coins) with the eight tints legible at a glance. Today about seven coins show, and only red, maroon and clear read.
The coins' rim highlights must be continuous, not the dotted or faceted specular dashes that give away the render.
The host-stand top must read as real oak at real scale, a darker stain with true grain, not pale, flat and stretched.
The frame must carry a sign that this is Planet EARF at its door (the etched name on the glass, the door frame), not an anonymous window.
No intersecting props: the matchbook at the bowl's foot passes under the bowl.

defects.what: Host-stand top front edge is the brightest large area (lum_median 133, p95 166), with a pale, washed oak and stretched, procedural-looking grain. It pulls the eye off the bowl.
Bowl interior is dark (lum_median 21, crush 9.8 %). Only about seven coins show, so a 'bowl of 40' reads as near empty, and the eight tints cannot be told apart.
Dark red coins have dotted, dashed specular rims (a beaded white line), a faceted-bevel or sampling artifact that reads as CG.
Black matchbook pokes out from under the bowl's foot and intersects it. It reads as a bracket or a clipping object rather than a matchbook set on the stand.
A flat, pale, featureless band beyond the glass (lum_median 122) is the second-brightest area and reads as an untextured plane, not a street or sill.
Two-thirds of the frame is unlit wall (lum_median 24, range 25). The board-form detail, tie holes and pour lines are barely visible, so the wall reads as dark flat panels.
Window upper area is flat grey-brown (range 15) with three bokeh discs. There is no etched name, no street life and no reflection of the room in the glass.
Faint, unreadable ghost shape in the glass (lum 62), neither a clean reflection nor the street.

changes.problem: The bowl, the subject, is darker than the timber it stands on and the street beyond. No pool of light lands in it.

evidence.measured: bowl lum_median 28.4 against shelf front [300,720,600,800] 132.8 and window band [820,510,1200,690] 121.7

change.setting: add a dedicated spot over the host stand (like the sink's: 1 x spot, 2700 K), aimed at the bowl's centre from high and slightly behind
change.from: none (the bowl is lit by spill)
change.to: 1 x spot, 12 W, 2600 K, cone 14 deg, blend 0.6, aimed into the bowl so the pool falls off across the stand within about 25 cm

changes.expected: The coins glow inside the copper and the bowl becomes the brightest mid-tone area, with the stand top falling off into shadow at its front edge.

changes.problem: The host-stand top is pale, flat and over-bright, with stretched grain that reads as a texture, not oak.

evidence.measured: lum_median 132.8, p95 166.2; the x profile peaks at 138 in the bin at x 450 to 525

change.to: a mid-dark smoked or fumed oak (base about #6B4A32), roughness 0.45 with a faint oiled sheen, grain scaled to real quarter-sawn oak (rays about 1 to 3 mm, boards 120 to 180 mm wide)

changes.expected: The stand top sits a stop or more below the bowl and reads as furniture-grade oak at real scale.

changes.problem: The street beyond the glass is a bright, flat, untextured band competing with the subject.

evidence.measured: lum_median 121.7, range limited, no texture visible at 2x

change.to: 2 x point, 70 W, 3000 K (a cooler sodium-to-LED street against the 2600 K room)

changes.expected: The street drops to a dim, slightly cooler backdrop with bokeh still readable, so the bowl wins.

changes.problem: The bowl reads as near empty, and the eight tints cannot be read: it does not look like a bowl of 40 coins.

evidence.measured: about seven coins visible, three hues (red, maroon, clear); crush 9.8 %

change.setting: props: brass bowl of EARFcoins at the door
change.from: 40 coins lying flat in a single layer, mostly hidden below the rim
change.to: 40 coins heaped above the rim in a loose mound (2 to 3 layers, some tilted on edge), all eight tints mixed so each shows at least twice from this camera, and two or three spilled onto the stand beside the bowl

changes.expected: A full, generous bowl with a visible spread of the eight tints catching the spot as small glowing edges.

changes.problem: The coins' rims carry dotted, beaded specular lines, the clearest render tell in the frame.

evidence.measured: at 2x, a broken white dash line along the rim of the dark red coins; clip 0.01 % in the bowl interior

change.setting: EARFcoin prop: edge geometry and finish
change.from: low-segment rim bevel, very low roughness
change.to: a rim of 96 or more segments with a smooth-shaded 0.5 mm round-over, polished-edge roughness 0.08, and clamp kept at 10

changes.expected: Continuous, thin, glowing polished edges, like cast acrylic, not dashed highlights.

changes.problem: The matchbook intersects the bowl's foot and reads as a bracket or a clipping object.

evidence.measured: at 4x, the black slab runs under the bowl's base, with no contact shadow on its far side

change.from: one passing under the bowl's foot at the left
change.to: both set flat on the stand top 3 to 5 cm clear of the bowl, one open with a match torn out, rotated about 15 deg off the stand's edge

changes.expected: A believable sign of life, with no intersection.

changes.problem: Half the frame is an unlit wall and a flat window, so the subject is small in a corner and nothing places it at Planet EARF's door.

evidence.measured: lum_median 24.3, range 24.8; the bowl takes about 5 % of the frame

change.to: lens 65 mm, f/2.8, moved back and lowered to about z 1.2 so the bowl fills the lower third, with the door's steel frame and the shopfront glass, its etched name readable in soft focus, filling the upper two thirds

changes.expected: The bowl is a third of the frame wide, and the shopfront and door identify the place.

changes.problem: The window's etched name is invisible, so there is no mark of the place, and the wall's board-form texture is lost in uniform dark.

change.setting: the window's etched name emission, plus haze
change.to: etched name 0.12; haze 0.006, so the stand's spot shows a faint cone and grazes the board-formed wall beside it

changes.expected: The name reads as soft glowing lettering in the glass, and the wall near the bowl shows board grain and tie holes.

out_of_scope.request: Put an Atmosphere speaker or an Orb lamp in this frame to carry EARF's colour
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the room's layout. Whether one is visible from the door depends on the camera within that layout, not on moving products.
